title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Given the level-order representation of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid Binary Search Tree (BST).
hints: Every node must fall strictly within a (minVal, maxVal) interval.

solutions.title: Recursive Range Validation
Inorder Monotonic Check

editorial.approach: Recursive DFS with range bounds (min_val, max_val): a node is valid if its value satisfies min_val < node.val < max_val. Recursively check that the left child satisfies (min_val, node.val) and the right child satisfies (node.val, max_val). Base case is null returning true. Initial bounds are (-infinity, +infinity).
editorial.why_optimal: Verifies all subtree invariants in O(N) time with O(H) call stack space, validating the global BST property rather than merely local child comparisons.
editorial.pitfalls: Only checking that node.left.val < node.val < node.right.val locally, which fails when a descendant violates an ancestor's bound (e.g. [5, 4, 6, null, null, 3, 7] where 3 is in 5's right subtree). Using fixed integer min/max constants as initial bounds instead of null or infinity, failing when node values equal INT_MIN or INT_MAX.
